explanation_chain: Satellite-only mode: no hydrometric gauge or HYDAT record was used; every quantity below is observable from space + terrain.
Terrain: HAND computed on the 30 m national DEM (MRDEM), channel scale 5.0 km2; this address sits 4.9 m above the nearest mapped channel.

Flood history: 38 years of optical water observations (JRC Global Surface Water, 1984-2021) were binned by HAND to give an empirical wet-probability curve for THIS reach; monotonicity in height is enforced (water cannot prefer higher ground).

The curve evaluated at the address's HAND gives the central annual probability 0.0%; the credible range 0.0%-6.4% combines within-band spread, spatial-correlation-deflated sample size, and the Bayesian posterior.
Observed flood extents: none available for this window yet — the estimate rests on the occurrence history alone.
Model constants: satellite-only defaults (occ_to_annual=1.0, px_decorr=25.0, prior_w=8, channel_km2=5.0)
Regional flood history (40 km window): the 38-year JRC occurrence record is a frequency, not a dated-event list; per-event flood history awaits the EGS extent connector (M-SAT-1).
mandatory_caveats: No in-situ gauge: the evidence grade is capped at C by construction. A gauged HazardWise report supersedes this one wherever it exists.

Optical occurrence under-counts short-duration and under-cloud floods, so the central probability is best read as a LOWER bound of that evidence channel; the upper credible bound carries that asymmetry.
SAR/optical water mapping is unreliable under dense canopy and in built-up cores; occurrence there reads low regardless of true flooding.
The occurrence-to-annual-probability mapping is an interim disclosed form (constant above); it is replaced, not tuned.
